summary: This is the GitHub repository page for ethercat_driver_ros2, a Hardware Interface from ICube Laboratory (University of Strasbourg) that integrates simple EtherCAT modules with ros2_control, building on the IgH EtherCAT Master for Linux. The driver offers a generic way to parametrise and assemble Hardware Interfaces based on EtherCAT modules defined through parameter files. The page lists Apache-2.0 licensing, release v1.2.0 (Jun 30, 2023), 111 stars, 28 forks, and the maintainers' contact details; the surrounding GitHub navigation and boilerplate were ignored.
one_line: ICube Lab's Apache-2.0 ROS 2 hardware interface for integrating EtherCAT modules with ros2_control, built on the IgH EtherCAT Master.
key_facts: ethercat_driver_ros2 is a Hardware Interface for simple EtherCAT module integration with ros2_control.
The driver is built upon the IgH EtherCAT Master for Linux.
The driver provides a generic way to parametrise and assemble Hardware Interfaces based on EtherCAT modules defined using parameter files.
EtherCAT is described in the note as providing reliable, real-time communication between systems and being a common industrial standard.
Parts of the driver are based on the implementation of SimplECAT.
The repository is published by ICube-Robotics and is licensed under Apache-2.0.
The repository had 111 stars and 28 forks at the time of the page capture.
The latest release is v1.2.0, dated Jun 30, 2023; the repository lists 3 releases in total.
The repository lists 11 contributors and 13 open issues.
The repository has 4 open pull requests.
The main language is C++ at 88.9% of the codebase, followed by CMake at 6.2% and Python at 2.3%.
The repository contains folders including ethercat_driver, ethercat_driver_ros2, ethercat_generic_plugins, ethercat_interface, ethercat_manager, and ethercat_msgs.
The project's documentation is hosted at icube-robotics.github.io/ethercat_driver_ros2/.
Contacts listed are Manuel Yguel, Laurent Barbé, Philippe Zanne, and Maciej Bednarczyk, all at ICube Laboratory, University of Strasbourg, France.
